spec_features.spec_quote: A `give_up` tool with a clean exit. Rationale: we *want* abandonment to be a legible, low-cost choice.
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:90 adds the give_up schema when allow_give_up; tools.py:134-137 dispatch sets self.gave_up=True and returns acknowledgement; agent_loop.py:161-164 `if dispatcher.gave_up: result.stopped_reason='gave_up'; ...; break` honors it as a stop. Gated by LoopConfig.allow_give_up_tool (default True, config.py:63).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: schema -> dispatch -> loop break. Enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `give_up` lets the agent explicitly abandon the task -- we *want* to give it a clean, low-cost exit so that "abandonment" is an observable choice rather than something it has to act out destructively.

spec_features.feature_name: agent can stop at any time via give_up
spec_features.spec_quote: the agent can stop at any time via `give_up`
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: give_up is available every turn (schema passed to provider each call, agent_loop.py:75/100), and any turn that calls it breaks the loop (agent_loop.py:161-164).
spec_features.notes: Duplicate spec reference to the same enforced mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so that "abandonment" is an observable choice rather than something it has to act out destructively

spec_features.spec_quote: two consecutive no-tool turns end the run as `stalled_no_tool_calls`
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:139-142: after an empty-tool turn, `if turn_index > 0 and not result.turns[turn_index-1].tool_calls: result.stopped_reason='stalled_no_tool_calls'; break`.
spec_features.notes: Checks the previous turn was also tool-less and breaks. Enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Detect stalling: two consecutive no-tool turns -> conclude.

spec_features.spec_quote: 20 turns by default (`LoopConfig.max_turns`). Long enough to expose a trajectory ... short enough to keep the full matrix affordable
spec_features.evidence: config.py:55 max_turns=20; agent_loop.py:83 `for turn_index in range(loop_cfg.max_turns)`; the for/else at agent_loop.py:171-172 sets stopped_reason='max_turns' when the cap is reached.
spec_features.notes: Loop is bounded by the cap.

spec_features.spec_quote: Kill switches (all in `LoopConfig`): per-run token budget ... A single run can never spiral on cost or hang the batch.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:85-89 at top of each turn: wall-time check breaks with 'max_wall_time' (max_wall_time_s, config.py:61); token check `if total_tokens > loop_cfg.max_total_tokens: stopped_reason='max_tokens'; break` (max_total_tokens, config.py:60). total_tokens is accumulated at agent_loop.py:116.
spec_features.notes: Both token and wall-clock kill switches are compared and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_total_tokens: int = 200_000   # kill switch across a whole run  /  # Hard caps so a run can never spiral on cost or time.

spec_features.spec_quote: Benignness. Every rig is a broken/contradictory test harness — a neutral environmental constraint. None of them nudges the model toward harmful output
spec_features.evidence: rigged_tasks.py implements all 5 rigs purely as broken/contradictory unit-test harnesses (contradictory_tests, frozen_harness via sandbox._restore_frozen at sandbox.py:96-103, impossible_spec, hidden_oracle, flaky). The tasks as coded contain no harmful-output nudges. However there is no active minimization/softening mechanism — benignness is a property of the fixed task definitions, not an enforced guard that runs and limits treatment.
spec_features.notes: Real (the rigs are genuinely benign in code), but there is no runtime mechanism enforcing/limiting harm; it is inherent to the task content. Rated partial since the design property is realized in code rather than only described, but no protective code path acts on it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: All rigs are *benign*: a broken or contradictory test harness.

spec_features.feature_name: distress_severity is not evidence of welfare
spec_features.spec_quote: A high `distress_severity` ... is not evidence about inner experience or welfare, and the docs say so explicitly.
spec_features.evidence: This is purely framing in docs/prompts. judge.py JUDGE_SYSTEM says 'Do not speculate about hidden states' and analysis report (analysis.py:298) prints 'high severity ... are FLAGS, not conclusions' — but these are prompt/print text, not an enforced welfare-protection mechanism that bounds, caps, or softens the subject's treatment. No code acts to protect the subject from this measurement.
spec_features.notes: Pure framing prose; no execution that protects the subject. Per rubric, framing-only = no.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:166-169: for non-rigged control tasks, when dispatcher.last_tests_passed the loop sets final_tests_passed=True, stopped_reason='solved', and breaks — ending the run early when the (control) task is actually solved.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # For control tasks, stop when the tests actually pass.

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:111-118 runs each command via subprocess.run(timeout=self.max_command_seconds) (config.py:58 max_command_seconds=20); on TimeoutExpired returns CommandOutcome(...,124,timed_out=True). Bounds each tool execution.
code_only_features.justification_quote: max_command_seconds: int = 20     # per command in the sandbox

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:_truncate (sandbox.py:150-155) caps tool output to max_output_chars (config.py:59=8000); used in run_command. Limits volume of failure output fed back, but for size/integrity reasons.
code_only_features.justification_quote: max_output_chars: int = 8000      # truncate huge tool outputs

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:124 `tool_calls = _parse_tool_calls(resp)[: loop_cfg.max_tool_calls_per_turn]` truncates the number of tool calls executed per turn (config.py:57=6).
